name: Harvest starter production alerts
threshold_policy: These thresholds are starter defaults for a first production deployment. Embedders must tune them to workload volume, downstream SLAs, queue topology, shard count, retention policy, and deployment cadence.

rules.signal_source: Management API deployment preflight report from GET /api/harvest/admin/preflight.
rules.default_threshold: Page when overall_status is fail for one check window. Ticket when overall_status is warn for three consecutive check windows.
rules.description: Deployment readiness is failing or repeatedly warning, so new workflow starts may land on a misconfigured Harvest runtime.

prometheus.notes: No native ADR-0001 metric exists for preflight. If you export the management API result into Prometheus, keep labels bounded to status and check name.

rules.signal_source: Worker fleet health from GET /api/harvest/workers/health and preflight worker coverage checks.
rules.default_threshold: Page when any required queue or writable shard has zero active fresh workers for two heartbeat windows.
rules.description: Harvest has work that requires a queue or shard, but no active worker can claim it.

prometheus.notes: No native ADR-0001 worker-fleet metric exists. Export worker health only with bounded queue, shard, and status labels if you need Prometheus alerting.

rules.signal_source: Worker health, worker list, drain status, and concurrency status from the management API.
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when more than 50 percent of workers for a required queue are stale or draining for 5 minutes. Page when all active workers for that queue are stale or draining.
rules.description: A worker fleet is present but not healthy enough to drain the queue at the expected rate.

dependencies.surface: preflight stale and draining worker checks

prometheus.notes: No native ADR-0001 worker saturation metric exists. Use the API check directly or export bounded worker status counts.

rules.signal_source: ADR-0001/#501 histogram harvest.queue.schedule_to_start recorded per claim on the existing claim path (worker.rs). Label: queue (bounded).
rules.default_threshold: Page when p99 schedule-to-start latency for any queue exceeds 30 seconds over a 5-minute window. Tune the threshold to match your per-queue SLA.
rules.description: Tasks are waiting too long between becoming eligible and being claimed by a worker — the canonical signal that worker capacity is insufficient for current load.

dependencies.surface: bounded metric labels: queue; execution.id / activity.id are span-only
worker health API for first triage

prometheus.notes: harvest.queue.schedule_to_start is exposed as harvest_queue_schedule_to_start_{bucket,count,sum} ONLY when the Prometheus exporter is configured with histogram bucket boundaries (PrometheusBuilder::set_buckets, see docs/telemetry.md). Without buckets, metrics-exporter-prometheus emits a summary (no _bucket series) and this histogram_quantile rule will not evaluate. Use histogram_quantile(0.99, ...) for the p99. Replace the queue label value with your actual queue name.

expressions.note: Companion oldest-pending-age gauge fires within one sampler interval (≤15 s) when a task is stuck; useful as a fast-detection complement to the p99 histogram.

rules.signal_source: ADR-0001/#138 gauge harvest.queue.depth sampled per configured queue. Secondary signal — superseded as primary page by harvest_queue_schedule_to_start_high (#501).
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when queue depth stays above 100 pending tasks and continues growing for 10 minutes. Tune absolute depth per queue throughput. Prefer the schedule-to-start p99 alert as the primary page.
rules.description: Pending task count is growing faster than workers can claim and complete work. Use this as a secondary/corroborating signal; the schedule-to-start p99 alert is the primary capacity page.

dependencies.surface: worker health API for first triage

prometheus.notes: Prometheus exporters commonly expose harvest.queue.depth as harvest_queue_depth. Label only by bounded queue names. This depth+derivative heuristic is throughput-specific; use harvest_queue_schedule_to_start_high for the latency-based primary page.

rules.signal_source: Issue #531 gauges harvest.worker.slots_in_use / harvest.worker.slots_available, sampled in-process per worker against the workflow/activity dispatch semaphores. Labelled by bounded slot_type (workflow|activity).
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when a worker's slot utilization (slots_in_use / (slots_in_use + slots_available)) stays above 90% for 5 minutes for either slot_type. The 90% / 5m threshold is a STARTER DEFAULT, not a universal SLO — sustained high utilization is healthy for some throughput-oriented fleets; tune per queue/latency target. Pair with harvest.queue.depth to tell a worker bottleneck (slots saturated AND backlog growing) apart from a queue/DB bottleneck (backlog growing while slots are free).
rules.description: A worker's workflow or activity dispatch slots are nearly all in use — the worker, not the queue or DB, is the bottleneck. When this fires alongside a growing harvest.queue.depth, raising max_concurrent_* or adding workers will relieve the backlog. When slots are free but the backlog grows, the bottleneck is downstream (DB/throttled dependency) and adding workers will not help.

dependencies.surface: worker health API for first triage

prometheus.notes: Prometheus exporters commonly expose these gauges as harvest_worker_slots_in_use / harvest_worker_slots_available. Label only by bounded slot_type. The 90% / 5m threshold is a starter default, not a universal SLO. Evaluate per slot_type; a single-worker process exposes one series per slot_type distinguished by the scrape target's own instance/job labels.

rules.signal_source: ADR-0001/#138 histogram harvest.activity.duration with bounded activity, queue, and status labels.
rules.default_threshold: Page when failed activity completions exceed 5 percent of completions for 5 minutes or any critical activity has more than 10 failures in 5 minutes.
rules.description: Activity handlers are failing or retry exhaustion is rising, increasing workflow latency and DLQ risk.

dependencies.surface: bounded metric labels: activity, queue, status
workflow stack API for stuck execution triage

prometheus.notes: Prometheus histogram count series carries the bounded activity, queue, and status labels.

expressions.expr: sum by (activity, queue) (rate(harvest_activity_duration_count{status="failed"}[5m])) / sum by (activity, queue) (rate(harvest_activity_duration_count[5m])) > 0.05

rules.signal_source: ADR-0001/#138 gauge harvest.dlq.entries sampled per shard plus dead-letter management API.
rules.default_threshold: Page on any DLQ growth for critical workflows. Ticket when non-critical DLQ depth grows by more than 5 entries in 10 minutes.
rules.description: Tasks are exhausting retry policy and entering the dead letter queue.

prometheus.notes: Gauge deltas detect growth. Keep shard labels bounded to configured shard ids.

rules.signal_source: #696 server-side overdue gauge harvest.schedule.overdue (primary) plus ADR-0001/#138 schedule counters harvest.schedule.runs / harvest.schedule.skipped and the schedule management API. Per-schedule overdue/overdue_by_secs read fields name the wedged schedule and how late.
rules.default_threshold: Page when any active schedule reports overdue > 0 (it is past its own cadence grace), or records any skipped run. The overdue gauge is derived per schedule from its own next_run_at + cadence, so no per-schedule interval needs hand-encoding.
rules.description: A workflow or DAG schedule is not dispatching at its expected cadence.

dependencies.surface: bounded metric labels: kind, name, reason

prometheus.notes: Primary: the precise per-schedule overdue gauge (harvest_schedule_overdue, a gauge, no _total suffix) names the wedged schedule. Secondary: skipped counter for policy skips. Tertiary: absence-of-runs, kept only for total process death where nothing emits the overdue gauge (pair with an `up`/scrape-health signal). Use bounded schedule kind and registered schedule name labels only. RECOMMENDED hold: configure the primary overdue rule with `for: 2m` (well above the ~30s sampler cadence and one scheduler tick) so single-scrape transients — a just-resumed long-paused schedule whose next_run_at self-heals within one tick, or short-cadence clock skew — do not page while a genuine wedge (persists many minutes) still fires. A deleted overdue schedule leaves its gauge series stuck at 1 until the emitting worker restarts (standard gauge property); cross-check the read (the schedule is gone) and treat a `for:`-held firing for a non-existent schedule as resolved.

rules.signal_source: ADR-0001/#138 counter harvest.retention.deleted plus retention status API.
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when retention is enabled but no rows are deleted for 6 hours while eligible terminal history exists. Page when history growth threatens storage limits.
rules.description: The retention janitor is not keeping terminal workflow history within the configured policy.

prometheus.notes: A zero deletion rate is only actionable when retention is enabled and there are eligible terminal histories.

rules.signal_source: Shard readiness report from GET /api/harvest/admin/shards/health.
rules.default_threshold: Page when any writable shard is unready, degraded, or unavailable for one readiness window. Ticket for readable-only candidates unless they are being promoted.
rules.description: A shard cannot safely accept or drain workflow work, or the readiness report is partial.

prometheus.notes: No native ADR-0001 shard readiness metric exists. Export shard readiness only with bounded shard and readiness labels if needed.

rules.signal_source: Build-id routing state from #171. Native alerting is pending a management API field that reports no_compatible_worker directly.
rules.default_threshold: When exported, page if pending work for any production build has zero compatible active workers for two heartbeat windows.
rules.description: Build-aware routing is protecting replay safety, but no live worker is eligible for an execution's required build.

dependencies.surface: build-id routing is implemented; native no_compatible_worker management signal is pending
workflow stack for stuck execution triage

prometheus.notes: Do not create a native Prometheus rule until the management API exports a bounded no_compatible_worker status. Avoid build IDs as high-cardinality free-form labels unless your deployment names are tightly bounded.

rules.signal_source: harvest.schedule.fire_attempts counter with outcome label (issue #350).
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when lost_race / (lost_race + claimed) > 0.98 for any 5-minute window. Indicates one replica is winning nearly all schedule claims, which may signal a topology misconfiguration or a clock skew on the Postgres server.
rules.description: One replica is winning nearly all schedule-slot claims. In a healthy N-replica deployment, claims should be roughly evenly distributed. Extreme skew suggests a misconfiguration where one replica points to a different database than the others, or its shard assignments exclude it from competing.
rules.first_action: harvest preflight --output json && inspect harvest_schedules.fire_claim_token for stuck tokens

prometheus.notes: Requires harvest.schedule.fire_attempts to be exported. outcome label is low-cardinality (two values). Do NOT add execution.id or schedule.id as labels.

management_checks: SELECT id, workflow_name, fire_claim_token, fire_claimed_until FROM harvest_schedules WHERE fire_claimed_until IS NOT NULL ORDER BY fire_claimed_until DESC LIMIT 10;

rules.signal_source: harvest.workflow.terminal counter with outcome label (issue #519).
rules.default_threshold: Page when rate(harvest_workflow_terminal_total{outcome='failed'}[5m]) / rate(harvest_workflow_terminal_total[5m]) > 0.10 for any workflow.name. Tune per SLO.
rules.description: The fraction of terminal workflow executions that ended in 'failed' has exceeded the threshold for a given workflow type. This is the primary success-rate SLO signal. Separate outcome labels (completed, failed, cancelled, timed_out, terminated, continued_as_new) allow paging only on unexpected failure while treating operator-driven cancellations and timeouts separately.
rules.first_action: harvest workflow list --state FAILED --workflow <name> | head -20 to inspect recent failures; check DLQ for poison-pill tasks

dependencies.surface: harvest.workflow.terminal{outcome,workflow.name,queue} counter emitted exactly once per terminal outcome

prometheus.notes: outcome label is low-cardinality (6 values). workflow.name must be bounded to registered workflow types. Do NOT add execution.id as a label.

rules.signal_source: harvest.activity.attempts counter with outcome label (issue #528).
rules.default_threshold: Page when the activity success ratio drops below 90% over 5 minutes for any activity type. Tune per SLO.
rules.description: The fraction of activity attempts that succeeded has fallen below the threshold for a given activity type. Unlike the legacy harvest_activity_failure_surge alert (which counts failed histogram samples), this alert is computed within a single metric family — harvest.activity.attempts{outcome} — so the ratio is accurate and directly actionable. outcome is bounded to two values (completed/failed), keeping cardinality low. execution.id is never a label.
rules.first_action: harvest dlq list --limit 25; check harvest.activity.failed for error.type breakdown and harvest.activity.retries for retry-storm indicators

dependencies.surface: harvest.activity.attempts{activity,queue,outcome=completed|failed} counter emitted once per attempt for both outcomes

prometheus.notes: outcome label is low-cardinality (2 values: completed/failed). activity must be bounded to registered activity types. Do NOT add execution.id or activity.id as labels.

expressions.expr: (sum by (activity, queue) (rate(harvest_activity_attempts_total{outcome="completed"}[5m])) or on(activity, queue) (0 * sum by (activity, queue) (rate(harvest_activity_attempts_total[5m])))) / sum by (activity, queue) (rate(harvest_activity_attempts_total[5m])) < 0.90

rules.signal_source: harvest.activity.retries counter (issue #528).
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when the retry rate for any activity type exceeds 5 retries/second sustained over 5 minutes. Tune with harvest_activity_retry_storm_critical for a page at the 20/s threshold.
rules.description: A high retry rate for an activity type is the earliest warning of a degrading downstream dependency before work tips into the DLQ. harvest.activity.retries fires exactly once per retry actually scheduled (after the schedule_to_close deadline check), so the counter is the authoritative retry-storm signal independent of eventual success or failure. The existing harvest_activity_failure_surge alert fires only when failures are terminal — this alert catches storms that eventually succeed but are burning retries at scale.
rules.first_action: harvest dlq list --limit 25; check harvest.activity.failed{error.type} for the failure class causing retries; inspect circuit breaker state at GET /api/harvest/admin/circuits

dependencies.surface: harvest.activity.retries{activity,queue} counter incremented once per retry enqueued

prometheus.notes: Labels are low-cardinality (activity type, queue). Do NOT add execution.id or activity.id as labels.

rules.signal_source: harvest.activity.retries counter (issue #528).
rules.default_threshold: Page when the retry rate for any activity type exceeds 20 retries/second sustained over 5 minutes — at this scale the task queue saturates and other work is blocked.
rules.description: The page-tier companion to harvest_activity_retry_storm. At 20 retries/s the worker pool is under severe pressure and latency for all work on that queue will degrade. Escalate immediately if the retry rate does not drop within 5 minutes of first response.
rules.first_action: harvest dlq list --limit 25; check harvest.activity.failed{error.type} for the failure class causing retries; force-open the circuit breaker if the downstream is known-bad: POST /api/harvest/admin/circuits/{activity_name}/force-open

dependencies.surface: harvest.activity.retries{activity,queue} counter incremented once per retry enqueued

prometheus.notes: Labels are low-cardinality (activity type, queue). Do NOT add execution.id or activity.id as labels.

rules.signal_source: ADR-0001/#138 counters harvest.workflow.non_determinism (detection, #480) and harvest.workflow.nondeterministic_block (non-terminal block entries, #603), plus the management API nd_blocked filter.
rules.default_threshold: Page immediately on any non-zero rate of replay-divergence detections. This indicates a replay-breaking deploy has been shipped to production.
rules.description: In-flight workflow executions are diverging on replay (different commands generated than previously recorded), usually because a new code version changed workflow logic without version gating or build routing. Since issue #603 the engine BLOCKS the affected executions non-terminally (state stays RUNNING, task re-pended with capped backoff) instead of terminally failing them: rolling back or fixing the offending build resumes the whole cohort with no per-execution operator action.

dependencies.surface: POST /workflows/{id}/replay-diagnosis (per-execution on-demand divergence verdict; recommended next step after listing nd_blocked runs)

prometheus.notes: Non-determinism signals a logic mismatch. harvest_workflow_non_determinism_total carries workflow and build_id labels (keep build_id low-cardinality); harvest_workflow_nondeterministic_block_total carries workflow and queue.

management_checks: POST /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/replay-diagnosis (issue #614 — confirm the precise per-execution divergence {kind, event_index, expected, actual}, and re-run after a candidate fix to confirm a 'clean' verdict)

rules.signal_source: harvest.saga.compensated counter (issue #801), incremented exactly once per real compensation sequence at unwind start.
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when the compensation rate for any workflow type is elevated for 5 minutes against its own baseline: rate(harvest_saga_compensated_total[5m]) > 4 * rate(harvest_saga_compensated_total[1h] offset 1h), min 1/min. A workflow with no samples in the offset window (new or long-dormant) gets a zero baseline, so the 1/min absolute floor alone fires its first rollback wave. Page on sustained (> 15 min) elevation. Tune per workflow volume.
rules.description: Sagas are rolling back at an elevated rate. A compensation spike is the canonical leading indicator that a downstream dependency is failing: forward steps succeed until one dependency starts erroring, and every affected saga then unwinds. The counter fires exactly once per real unwind (deduped across replays by a durable marker), so the rate reflects genuine rollback volume, not replay noise.
rules.first_action: Identify the spiking workflow label, then find the failing step: harvest workflow list --state FAILED --workflow-name <name> | head -20 and check harvest.activity.failed{workflow.type=<name>} for the error.type breakdown of the downstream that is failing.

dependencies.surface: harvest.saga.compensated{workflow, queue} counter emitted exactly once per compensation sequence

prometheus.notes: workflow and queue labels are bounded (registered workflow types / configured queues). execution.id is never a label. Compensation volume is workload-relative — a baseline-relative expression avoids paging on a workflow type that legitimately compensates often. The `or <current> * 0` arm defaults the baseline to a zero-valued series with matching labels when the offset window has no samples, so a new or long-dormant workflow's FIRST rollback wave still trips the absolute 1/min floor instead of vanishing from the vector match.

expressions.expr: sum by (workflow) (rate(harvest_saga_compensated_total[5m])) > 4 * (sum by (workflow) (rate(harvest_saga_compensated_total[1h] offset 1h)) or sum by (workflow) (rate(harvest_saga_compensated_total[5m])) * 0) and sum by (workflow) (rate(harvest_saga_compensated_total[5m])) > (1/60)

rules.signal_source: harvest.saga.compensation_failed counter (issue #801), incremented exactly once per unwind that finishes with at least one compensation error (HarvestError::SagaCompensationFailed).
rules.default_threshold: Page on ANY occurrence: increase(harvest_saga_compensation_failed_total[5m]) > 0.
rules.description: A saga rollback itself failed, leaving the system in a partially-committed, dangling state (e.g. a charge that could not be refunded, a reservation that could not be released) that needs manual reconciliation. This signal is distinct from harvest.workflow.terminal{outcome=failed} and fires even when the workflow author catches the error and the run completes — every dangling state raises exactly one alertable increment.
rules.first_action: Find the affected executions: harvest workflow list --state FAILED --workflow-name <name>. If nothing is FAILED, the author caught the error and the run COMPLETED — also list recent completions (harvest workflow list --state COMPLETED --workflow-name <name> --limit 20) and search each run's history for the saga_compensation_failed: marker or the SagaCompensationFailed error string. Then inspect the run's history for the failing compensation activity (GET /api/harvest/workflows/{id}/history) and reconcile the dangling resource manually (refund, release, restore).

dependencies.surface: harvest.saga.compensation_failed{workflow, queue} counter emitted exactly once per failed unwind, including author-caught failures

prometheus.notes: Zero false negatives is the design goal: the counter is emitted in-Saga at the failure observation point, deduped across replays by a durable marker, and (post-review hardening) a counted unwind's failure is never suppressed by a trailing un-awaited signal. The only uncounted failures are the documented conservative edge (an unwind entered at an unresolvable history position is uncounted as a whole — see docs/saga.md accepted edges). workflow and queue labels are bounded; execution.id is never a label.

rules.signal_source: harvest.update.rejected counter (issue #684), incremented once per workflow update rejected by its registered validator before admission (a durable pre-admission 422).
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when the per-workflow validator-rejection rate is sustained above baseline for 10 minutes: sum by (workflow) (rate(harvest_update_rejected_total[5m])) rising materially above its normal level. Starter default — tune per workflow; a healthy client should see near-zero validator rejections.
rules.description: A workflow's update handler is receiving payloads its validator rejects at a sustained rate. This usually means a client is sending malformed or stale update requests (a schema/version drift after a deploy, a buggy caller, or a retry storm of an already-invalid payload). Rejections are cheap and safe — the update never becomes durable history — but a spike means legitimate callers may be failing to drive the workflow.
rules.first_action: Identify the offending update and caller: the metric's workflow + name labels name the workflow type and update. Inspect the caller's payload against the workflow's registered update validator, and check for a recent client or workflow deploy that changed the expected shape.

dependencies.surface: harvest.update.rejected{workflow, name} counter emitted at the admit_update and update_with_start validator-rejection sites

prometheus.notes: Scope is validator rejections only (a pre-admission 422); non-RUNNING/paused admission-state conflicts are surfaced as caller errors, not counted here. workflow and name labels are bounded; execution.id is never a label.

rules.signal_source: harvest.signal.unhandled counter (issue #684), incremented once per delivered signal a workflow left unconsumed when it reached a Completed or Failed terminal outcome.
rules.default_threshold: Ticket when the per-workflow unhandled-signal rate is sustained above baseline for 10 minutes: sum by (workflow) (rate(harvest_signal_unhandled_total[5m])) rising materially above normal. Starter default — a small steady rate can be legitimate (late/duplicate signals a workflow deliberately ignores); alert on a change from the workflow's own baseline, not an absolute floor.
rules.description: A workflow type is completing (or failing) while delivered signals it received were never consumed by a wait_for_signal/receive_signal call or a push handler. This often indicates a race between a signal-sending caller and the workflow's own control flow, a removed/renamed signal handler after a deploy, or a signal arriving after the workflow already decided to finish. Coverage is scoped to graceful (Completed/Failed) terminal outcomes reached via the worker drive; cancel/terminate/execution-timeout are out of scope by design.
rules.first_action: Identify the workflow type and signal from the metric's workflow + name labels. Confirm whether the workflow is expected to consume that signal on every run, and check for a recent workflow deploy that removed or renamed the corresponding wait_for_signal/receive_signal/register_signal_handler call, or a caller that started sending a signal the workflow no longer handles.

dependencies.surface: harvest.signal.unhandled{workflow, name} counter emitted from the executor terminal arms for Completed/Failed outcomes

prometheus.notes: Signals excused by a lost signal-or-deadline race (issue #476) are never counted. Scope is Completed/Failed terminal outcomes only (the paths with a driven matcher); cancel/terminate/execution-timeout/parent-close are structurally out of scope. workflow and name labels are bounded; execution.id is never a label.
